factsheet_lines_1_indexed.2: - Captain Bernard Thrush: Reclusive sailor and owner of the longboat, disappeared mysteriously.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.3: - Windmere Maritime Museum: Institution established to preserve artifacts and history related to the longboat mystery.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.4: - Norse Historians Association: Group of scholars interested in Norse history and legends, involved in the investigation.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.5: - Treasure Hunters’ Guild: Organization of individuals dedicated to seeking hidden treasures, drawn to Windmere.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.6: - Windmere Local Authorities: Law enforcement and government officials involved in the investigation.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.7: - Professor Ingrid Nilsen: Renowned historian specializing in Norse mythology, consulted for expertise on the brass ring.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.10: - Discovery of the Longboat (1926): The abandoned longboat is found adrift near Windmere, sparking national intrigue.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.11: - Examination of the Brass Ring (1926): Historians and treasure hunters analyzed the ring, believing it to hold the key to a hidden treasure.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.12: - Disappearance of Captain Thrush (1926): Weeks before the longboat’s discovery, Captain Thrush vanished, leaving behind cryptic notes.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.13: - Nationwide Treasure Hunts (1926-1927): Inspired by the ring and its potential secrets, treasure hunts were launched along Windmere's coast.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.14: - Establishment of Windmere Maritime Museum (1928): Museum founded to collect and display artifacts from the longboat mystery and related Viking lore.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.17: - Windmere: Small coastal town where the longboat was discovered.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.18: - Windmere Shores: Area along the coast where treasure hunts were concentrated.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.19: - Thrush's Cottage: The secluded residence of Captain Thrush, where his notes were found.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.20: - North Sea Routes: Referenced in Captain Thrush’s notes as ancient Norse pathways.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.23: - 1926: Year the longboat was found and the mystery began.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.24: - Late 1926: Period of Captain Thrush's disappearance and the initial frenzy over the brass ring.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.25: - 1926-1927: Timeframe during which treasure hunts and public fascination peaked.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.26: - 1928: Year the Windmere Maritime Museum was established.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.29: - Captain Thrush’s Obsession: Thrush was believed to be obsessed with Norse lore and legends, motivating his journey on ancient routes.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.30: - Brass Ring as a Clue: The ring’s Norse symbols hinted at a connection to Viking artifacts and legends, prompting treasure hunts and scholarly interest.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.31: - Cultural Fascination: The public and academic interest in the mystery was fueled by a growing fascination with Norse mythology and legendary treasures.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.32: - Preservation of History: The establishment of the Windmere Maritime Museum was driven by a desire to document and preserve the enigmatic events and artifacts for future generations.

items.instruction: Under the confirmation rules a preserved unit (assertion_only or conflict_flagged) must be its own group, and that group's statement must be the unit's source_statement copied verbatim, with no added or removed punctuation. Fix it in one of two ways. (a) Only for assertion_only: if an exact factsheet line supports the assertion as stated, set status "grounded", give the exact line(s) as evidence, and say why in "note". The unit may then stay in its group. (b) Otherwise give the unit its own group: a new id ground-<event>-<nn> with an unused nn, source_unit_ids [the unit], statement = source_statement verbatim, and a grouping_rationale. Remaining members keep their group. Every distinct answer label of every group must have exactly one source_qa record with two closed-book questions (AUTHORING-SPEC.md). Move, keep or write source_qa records so this holds, with unit_id set to the record's group id. For this item, option (b) means setting this group's statement to the source_statement verbatim. Then check that its source_qa questions still follow the rules.
